title: copyparty
name: copyparty
description: File server in one Python app, with resumable uploads, thumbnails, search and a music player in the browser, plus WebDAV for mounting it as a drive. Source: https://github.com/9001/copyparty

env.name: COPYPARTY_PASSWORD
env.label: Password (required)
env.description: What you'll log in with. Anything long and hard to guess, or generate one with: openssl rand -hex 16

env.name: COPYPARTY_PORT
env.label: Host port for the web UI

note: Set the password before you deploy, since the stack won't start without one. Then open http://<your-host>:3923 (or whichever port you picked) and you'll land on a login box that only wants the password, no username. Logged in, you can upload, make folders, move, delete and see everything, while anyone else just gets that login box (upstream's own default is read-write for everyone). Files live in the copyparty-files volume, and the search index, thumbnails and logins live in copyparty-config. WebDAV clients connect to the same address, with any username and that password. Its switch to https button uses a certificate built into every copyparty, so it's no real protection, and a reverse proxy is the way to get proper HTTPS. Docs: github.com/9001/copyparty
